input.content:
Credit Control

Credit control in webERP applies the same rules to every customer, every time, whichever way an order arrives, and keeps a history of every credit decision for the auditors. It covers credit reviews, putting customers on stop or on watch, holding orders that take a customer over their credit limit, reminder letters, month end interest and late fees, bad debt write offs, the credit control report and the month end reconciliation of the customer accounts with the general ledger.

Overview and who can do what

The credit control screens are on the Receivables (AR) menu. Two security tokens control who can act:

  • Credit control (token 21) - the credit controller and the deputy. They can record credit reviews, change credit limits and the credit status (stop, watch, normal), release held orders, run the reminder letters, post and waive month end charges, write off bad debts within the approval limit and load the credit status from a spreadsheet. Give the same role to the credit controller and the deputy so that both have the same powers and see the same history.
  • Credit control approvals (token 22) - the Finance Director. Approves or rejects write offs over the approval limit. A write off can never be approved by the person who asked for it.

Finance sets the parameters (review periods, interest rate, late fee, GL accounts, approval limit) in Credit Control Settings, which needs the general ledger configuration token (10).

Nobody else can change a credit limit or a credit status: the customer maintenance screen shows them read only, the credit status codes can only be maintained by credit control, and the API refuses changes from users without the token. Sales reps (users set up with a sales person) can see the credit position, history and reminders of their own customers only, and cannot change anything.

If both the credit controller and the deputy are away, the system administrator can give the credit control token to another person's role for the period in User Roles (WWW_Access.php). Every action is recorded against the user who did it.

For sales staff - watch and stop

On watch: the customer can still be supplied. When you take an order you will see a warning, the order is accepted and credit control can see it. Talk to the customer about their account if you can.

On stop: no new orders can be taken for the customer - not by the sales office, the web shop, EDI or standing (recurring) orders - and goods cannot be picked, dispatched or invoiced on orders taken before the stop. The customer's account shows the reason. Quotations can still be prepared.

Over the credit limit: an order that takes the customer over their credit limit (account balance plus open orders) is accepted but held for credit approval. It cannot be picked, dispatched or invoiced until credit control releases it.

In all cases contact credit control. Nobody outside credit control can override a stop, a hold or a credit limit.

Setting up credit control

Credit Control Settings (AR maintenance) holds:

  • Standard review period (months, normally 12) and the shorter review period for customers on watch or stop (normally 6). New customers get a next review date when the account is opened.
  • Hold orders that take a customer over their credit limit.
  • The credit status codes used for normal, watch and stop. The stop code is used when a customer is put on stop automatically after a write off.
  • The interest rate (% per annum, charged monthly at a twelfth of the rate), the late fee (a fixed amount per month in home currency, converted to the customer's currency) and the days overdue before an item is charged. Zero switches interest or the fee off.
  • The GL accounts for interest income, late fee income and bad debts.
  • The write off approval limit in home currency.
  • The minimum days between reminder letters to the same customer and the email address the letters are sent from.

Reminder Letter Stages (AR maintenance) holds the stages of the reminder letters: the number of days overdue that trigger each stage, the email subject and the wording. Three stages are supplied: a polite reminder at 30 days, a second reminder at 45 days and a final notice at 60 days. The wording can use {CustomerName}, {AccountNo}, {Currency}, {OverdueAmount}, {InvoiceList}, {CompanyName} and {Date}. Mark the last stage as the final notice. Letters are in one language.

Reminder letters go to the customer's accounts contacts - the contacts flagged to receive statements in the customer contacts. Make sure each customer has one with a valid email address.

Going live - loading the stop list

When credit control goes live every existing customer keeps their current credit status code and balances. To load the current stop list, watch list, credit limits and review dates from the credit control spreadsheet use Import Customer Credit Status (AR maintenance) with a csv file of: customer code, status (normal, watch, stop or a status code), credit limit, next review date (YYYY-MM-DD), reason. Blank columns leave the value unchanged. The file is checked first and nothing is loaded if any line is wrong. Each change is recorded in the customer's credit history.

Customers without a next review date show on the credit control report as due for review. Set a date for all of them at once from Credit Control Settings.

Credit reviews

Customer Credit Control (AR transactions, or from the selected customer's menu) shows the customer's credit status, limit, balance, open orders, overdue amount, amount over the limit, next review date, outstanding items, reviews, held orders, reminders, charges and the full credit history.

To record a review choose the outcome (limit confirmed, raised or reduced, put on watch, put on stop, returned to normal), the credit limit, the credit status, the next review date (defaulted from the review periods) and the notes. The limit and status change as part of the review so the decision and its reason are always recorded together. Reviews cannot be changed or deleted.

Stop and watch

Put a customer on stop or watch, or back to normal, from Customer Credit Control by choosing the new credit status code and giving a reason. Each change records who made it, when and why. The status is shown wherever staff look at the customer: the customer selection screen, the account inquiry, the account statement, order entry and dispatch.

The customer's interest and late fee exemptions (for example key accounts or agreed payment plans) are set on the same screen, with a reason. Notes such as a promise to pay, or that a debt has gone to a collection agency or to court, can be added to the credit history.

Orders held for credit approval

Credit Held Orders lists the orders that cannot be dispatched: orders held because they took the customer over their limit and open orders of customers on stop. Tick the orders to release, give a reason and release them. If a released order is later increased so that the customer is over the limit again it is held again. The screen also lists the orders taken for customers on watch.

Orders from the web shop that are held are accepted and the customer is told the order is awaiting approval. Customers on stop see in the web shop that their account is on hold and that they should contact credit control. EDI orders from customers on stop are not created and the EDI advice says why. Standing orders are not raised for customers on stop; they are raised by the first run after the customer comes off stop.

Disputed invoices

In Customer Credit Control mark an outstanding invoice as disputed with a reason. Disputed items are left out of reminder letters and are not charged interest until the dispute is marked as settled.

The reminder letter run

Run Reminder Letter Run (normally weekly). Select the currency and sales person if needed and preview. The preview shows each customer due a letter, the stage, the oldest item's days overdue, the overdue amount and where the letter will go. Untick customers who should not get a letter this time (a promise to pay, a dispute being discussed) and send.

  • Only undisputed items overdue by at least the stage's days are chased, net of payments and credits not yet allocated - a customer who has paid gets nothing.
  • A customer moves up one stage at a time, and only while the items in the last letter are still unpaid. New overdue items after everything was paid start again at the first stage.
  • Nobody gets two letters within the minimum days between letters.
  • Letters show the customer's own currency and list the overdue items.

Letters are emailed to the accounts contacts. Customers with no email address, and any emails that fail, are listed with a link to print the letter for posting. Every letter is recorded against the customer with the date, stage, items and amount, and can be seen on the customer's account and in the customer portal. Customers sent the final notice who are still overdue are listed on the credit control report so you can decide whether to put them on stop - the system does not stop them automatically.

Month end interest and late fees

After the month end, run Month End Interest and Late Fees, choose the month and preview. Customers with undisputed items overdue by at least the days set at the month end are charged:

  • Interest on the overdue balance (net of unallocated payments and credits, and not on earlier interest or fees) at a twelfth of the annual rate.
  • One late fee per customer per month.

Exempt customers are not charged. Untick any charge you do not want and post. Charges are raised in the customer's currency as separate items (Interest Charge and Late Payment Fee) with a description, appear on the account and the next statement, and post to the debtors control account and the income accounts set by Finance. A month cannot be charged twice: customers already charged for the month are left out if the run is repeated.

To waive a charge, find it in the list of charges for the month, give a reason and waive it. The waiver is a credit at the charge's own rate, allocated to the charge, and reverses the income in the general ledger. A charge that has already been paid cannot be waived - raise a credit note instead.

Bad debt write offs

In Bad Debt Write Off select the customer, enter the amount to write off against each unpaid item (all or part), give a reason and choose whether to put the customer on stop (the default). A write off up to the approval limit is posted straight away. A larger one is sent to the Finance Director, who approves or rejects it in Approve Bad Debt Write Offs; nothing changes on the account until it is approved.

The write off is a credit in the customer's currency, debiting the bad debt account, allocated against the items written off. Any difference between today's exchange rate and the rate of the original invoice is posted as an exchange difference, so the debtors control account still agrees with the customer accounts.

If a written off debt is later paid, record the recovery against the write off (Record Recovery). This puts the amount back on the customer's account, crediting the bad debt account, so the receipt can be allocated against it in the usual way.

The Bad Debt Write Off Report lists write offs over a period with the customer, amount, reason, who asked for it and who approved it.

Credit control report

The Credit Control Report lists customers due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit and by how much, and customers on watch or on stop (and those sent a final notice). It can be filtered by sales person and currency, and totals are shown in home currency. Sales reps only see their own customers. The aged debtors report also shows each customer's credit status, credit limit and last reminder stage.

Month end - reconciling the debtors control account

After the month end charges, waivers and write offs have been posted, run Debtors Control Reconciliation for the month. It compares the total of the customer accounts in home currency with the debtors control account in the general ledger. If they do not agree it shows the difference by transaction type, the customer transactions whose general ledger entries do not agree and the entries to the debtors control account that have no customer transaction (for example manual journals to the control account).

The credit control history

Every credit control action - account opening, reviews, status and limit changes, held and released orders, disputes, reminders, charges, waivers, write off requests, approvals and rejections, write offs, recoveries and notes - is recorded in the customer's credit control history with the date, the user and the reason. The history is shown in Customer Credit Control and cannot be changed. A customer with credit control history cannot be deleted.

The customer portal

Customers who log in see in their account status the reminder letters sent to them (which they can open) and the interest and fees charged, with their balance. They only ever see their own account. They see whether their account is on hold, but not the watch status or the reasons recorded by credit control.

Credit Held Orders lists the orders that cannot be dispatched: orders held because they took the customer over their limit and open orders of customers on stop. Tick the orders to release, give a reason and release them. If a released order is later increased so that the customer is over the limit again it is held again. The screen also lists the orders taken for customers on watch.

Orders from the web shop that are held are accepted and the customer is told the order is awaiting approval. Customers on stop see in the web shop that their account is on hold and that they should contact credit control. EDI orders from customers on stop are not created and the EDI advice says why. Standing orders are not raised for customers on stop; they are raised by the first run after the customer comes off stop.

Disputed invoices

In Customer Credit Control mark an outstanding invoice as disputed with a reason. Disputed items are left out of reminder letters and are not charged interest until the dispute is marked as settled.

The reminder letter run

Run Reminder Letter Run (normally weekly). Select the currency and sales person if needed and preview. The preview shows each customer due a letter, the stage, the oldest item's days overdue, the overdue amount and where the letter will go. Untick customers who should not get a letter this time (a promise to pay, a dispute being discussed) and send.

  • Only undisputed items overdue by at least the stage's days are chased, net of payments and credits not yet allocated - a customer who has paid gets nothing.
  • A customer moves up one stage at a time, and only while the items in the last letter are still unpaid. New overdue items after everything was paid start again at the first stage.
  • Nobody gets two letters within the minimum days between letters.
  • Letters show the customer's own currency and list the overdue items.

Letters are emailed to the accounts contacts. Customers with no email address, and any emails that fail, are listed with a link to print the letter for posting. Every letter is recorded against the customer with the date, stage, items and amount, and can be seen on the customer's account and in the customer portal. Customers sent the final notice who are still overdue are listed on the credit control report so you can decide whether to put them on stop - the system does not stop them automatically.

Month end interest and late fees

After the month end, run Month End Interest and Late Fees, choose the month and preview. Customers with undisputed items overdue by at least the days set at the month end are charged:

  • Interest on the overdue balance (net of unallocated payments and credits, and not on earlier interest or fees) at a twelfth of the annual rate.
  • One late fee per customer per month.

Exempt customers are not charged. Untick any charge you do not want and post. Charges are raised in the customer's currency as separate items (Interest Charge and Late Payment Fee) with a description, appear on the account and the next statement, and post to the debtors control account and the income accounts set by Finance. A month cannot be charged twice: customers already charged for the month are left out if the run is repeated.

To waive a charge, find it in the list of charges for the month, give a reason and waive it. The waiver is a credit at the charge's own rate, allocated to the charge, and reverses the income in the general ledger. A charge that has already been paid cannot be waived - raise a credit note instead.

Bad debt write offs

In Bad Debt Write Off select the customer, enter the amount to write off against each unpaid item (all or part), give a reason and choose whether to put the customer on stop (the default). A write off up to the approval limit is posted straight away. A larger one is sent to the Finance Director, who approves or rejects it in Approve Bad Debt Write Offs; nothing changes on the account until it is approved.

The write off is a credit in the customer's currency, debiting the bad debt account, allocated against the items written off. Any difference between today's exchange rate and the rate of the original invoice is posted as an exchange difference, so the debtors control account still agrees with the customer accounts.

If a written off debt is later paid, record the recovery against the write off (Record Recovery). This puts the amount back on the customer's account, crediting the bad debt account, so the receipt can be allocated against it in the usual way.

The Bad Debt Write Off Report lists write offs over a period with the customer, amount, reason, who asked for it and who approved it.

Credit control report

The Credit Control Report lists customers due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit and by how much, and customers on watch or on stop (and those sent a final notice). It can be filtered by sales person and currency, and totals are shown in home currency. Sales reps only see their own customers. The aged debtors report also shows each customer's credit status, credit limit and last reminder stage.

Month end - reconciling the debtors control account

After the month end charges, waivers and write offs have been posted, run Debtors Control Reconciliation for the month. It compares the total of the customer accounts in home currency with the debtors control account in the general ledger. If they do not agree it shows the difference by transaction type, the customer transactions whose general ledger entries do not agree and the entries to the debtors control account that have no customer transaction (for example manual journals to the control account).

The credit control history

Every credit control action - account opening, reviews, status and limit changes, held and released orders, disputes, reminders, charges, waivers, write off requests, approvals and rejections, write offs, recoveries and notes - is recorded in the customer's credit control history with the date, the user and the reason. The history is shown in Customer Credit Control and cannot be changed. A customer with credit control history cannot be deleted.

The customer portal

Customers who log in see in their account status the reminder letters sent to them (which they can open) and the interest and fees charged, with their balance. They only ever see their own account. They see whether their account is on hold, but not the watch status or the reasons recorded by credit control.

# Credit control – implementation notes

This is the credit control capability from `task/brd.md`. It covers credit reviews, stop and watch, credit holds on orders from every route, reminder letters, month-end interest and fees, bad-debt write-offs with approval, reporting, the customer portal, month-end reconciliation, install/upgrade, and the staff guide.

## How it fits webERP

webERP already had a credit status. Each customer has a hold reason (`debtorsmaster.holdreason` → `holdreasons`). The hold reason's `dissallowinvoices` flag means **1 = on stop** and **2 = watch**. Anything else (0, or the table default −1) means normal.

Order entry, `CustomerAccount`, `AgedDebtors` ("held only") and the API already read this flag. I kept it as the one source of truth rather than adding a parallel status. Credit control moves customers between hold reasons, and every move goes through one function that records who, when and why.

All the shared logic is in `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php`. Every route and page calls it, so the rules are applied the same way everywhere.

## What was built

### New tables

Each table is in `install/sql/tables/` and also in `sql/updates/44.php`:

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `custcreditreviews` | Credit reviews (immutable). |
| `custcreditevents` | Per-customer credit control history / audit trail (BR-32). |
| `creditorderholds` | One row per order that is held (over limit / stop), released, or noted (watch). |
| `dunningstages` | Reminder stages. |
| `dunningletters` | Letters sent. |
| `dunninglettertrans` | The items each letter covered. |
| `debtortransdisputes` | Disputed invoices. |
| `creditcharges` | Month-end charges. A unique key on (customer, period, type) stops a month being charged twice. |
| `creditwriteoffs`, `creditwriteoffitems` | Write-off requests, approvals and postings. |

New columns on `debtorsmaster`: `nextreviewdate`, `interestexempt`, `feeexempt`.

### New transaction types (`systypes`)

| Type | Name |
|---|---|
| 13 | Interest Charge |
| 14 | Late Payment Fee |
| 45 | Credit Control Charge Waiver |
| 46 | Bad Debt Write Off |
| 47 | Bad Debt Recovered |

They are separate types so that charges appear on accounts and statements as clearly described items (BR-21). It also stops them being mistaken for invoices: `PrintCustTrans` and `Z_SalesIntegrityCheck` assume a type 10 has a sales order.

### New security tokens

- **21 Credit control** – the credit controller and deputy.
- **22 Credit control approvals** – the Finance Director.

### New pages

All pages are on the AR menu and registered in `scripts`.

| Page | Token | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `CreditControl.php` | 2 | Customer credit hub. Shows position and history. Credit control can record reviews, change status, set exemptions, mark disputes and add notes. Reps see their own customers only, read-only. |
| `CreditOrderHolds.php` | 21 | Held orders, orders of stopped customers, and watch orders. Credit control releases orders here. |
| `DunningStages.php` | 21 | Stages, days overdue and wording. |
| `DunningRun.php` | 21 | Preview, exclude, send by email; customers without email are listed to post. |
| `DunningLetter.php` | 1 | View or print a letter. A customer login sees only its own. |
| `CreditCharges.php` | 21 | Preview and post month-end interest and fees; waive a charge. |
| `CreditWriteOff.php` | 21 | Write-off request or post, put on stop, record a recovery. |
| `CreditWriteOffApprove.php` | 22 | Approve or reject write-offs over the limit. |
| `CreditWriteOffReport.php` | 21 | BR-29. |
| `CreditControlReport.php` | 2 | BR-30. |
| `CreditControlSettings.php` | 10 | Finance's parameters, plus bulk next-review dates for go-live. |
| `CreditStatusImport.php` | 21 | Loads the spreadsheet stop list, limits and review dates (BR-40). |
| `DebtorsControlReconciliation.php` | 8 | BR-37/38. |

### Staff guide

- New `doc/Manual/ManualCreditControl.html` covers every 4.1 item and includes a "For sales staff" section (BR-43).
- Added to `ManualOutline.php`.
- `ManualCreditStatus.html` is updated.

## Existing code changed, and why

### Order routes (BR-06/08/10/11)

- **`DeliveryDetails.php`** is the single commit point for sales-office and web-shop orders.
  - It refuses orders for customers on stop. Quotations are still allowed.
  - After insert or update it calls `EvaluateOrderCredit()`, which holds an order that takes the customer over the limit and notes an order for a watch customer.
  - Customer logins get "awaiting approval" or "account on hold" messages.
- **`SelectOrderItems.php`**
  - Shows the status banner, including when modifying an order.
  - Web-shop customers on stop are told and stopped.
  - Watch is no longer shown to customers.
  - The customer-login path tested `dissallowinvoices == 0`. That treated the default −1 as "on hold", so I changed it to `!= 1`.
- **`ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`**, **`GeneratePickingList.php`**, **`PDFPickingList.php`**
  - These refuse or skip orders that are held, or whose customer is on stop, unless credit control has released the order.
  - `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` checks again at posting time.
- **`RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php`**
  - Skips templates of stopped customers without advancing `lastrecurrence`, so the order is raised on the first run after the stop is lifted.
  - Evaluates new orders, and does not auto-invoice a held order.
- **`EDIProcessOrders.php`**
  - Does not create orders for stopped customers, says why in the advice email, and logs it.
  - Evaluates created orders.
- **API**
  - `api_php.php` includes the library.
  - New error codes 1174–1176.
  - `InsertSalesOrderHeader` refuses stopped customers.
  - `InsertSalesOrderLine` and `ModifySalesOrderLine` evaluate the order and return `OrderHeldForCreditApproval` in `$Errors[1]` when it is held.
  - `InvoiceSalesOrder` refuses held or stopped orders.
  - `InsertCustomer` sets the next review date.
  - `ModifyCustomer` only lets token-21 users change `creditlimit` or `holdreason`, and records the change.

### Who may change limits and status (BR-07/34)

- **`Customers.php`**
  - Limit and credit status are read-only without token 21. Changes made by credit control go through the logging functions.
  - New customers get a next review date (BR-02) and an "opened" history entry.
  - A customer with credit history cannot be deleted.
- **`CreditStatus.php`**
  - Moved to token 21. The codes decide who is stopped.
  - A Normal/Watch/Stop select replaces the checkbox. The checkbox could only store 0/1, so saving a watch code silently reset it to normal.

### Visibility (BR-09/31/33/35/36)

- **`SelectCustomer.php`**: status banner and a link to Credit Control.
- **`CustomerInquiry.php`** and **`CustomerAccount.php`**
  - Status banner. "ACCOUNT ON HOLD" now shows only for status 1; it showed for watch and −1 too.
  - A customer login is forced to its own `www_users.customerid`. Before this, a customer could pass any `?CustomerID=` (BR-36).
  - Customers do not see watch or the reasons.
- **`CustomerAccount.php`** (also the portal "Account Status" page)
  - It only rendered types 10/11/12, so it now lists other types too (charges, waivers, write-offs).
  - New sections for reminder letters sent and charges (BR-35).
- **`AgedDebtors.php`**: credit status, credit limit and last reminder columns.

### Ledger agreement (BR-37/38)

`Z_CheckDebtorsControl.php` only counted types 10/11/12, so the new types would have shown as differences. It now has an "Other" column. The new reconciliation page is the main tool.

### Other existing files

- **`Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php`**: copies the new `debtorsmaster` columns and renames the new tables.
- **`Z_ImportDebtors.php`**: imported customers get a next review date.

## Install and upgrade (BR-39/40)

Following the map's hazard that schema lives in several places, each change is in all of them:

- **`sql/updates/44.php`**: tables, columns, systypes, tokens, scripts, config, menu items and reminder stages. It is guarded by `Errors == 0`.
  - Tokens 21/22 go to every role that already holds token 15 (administrators). The administrator then assigns them to the credit controllers' and Finance Director's roles.
  - It reuses existing watch, stop and normal hold reasons if the company has them, and creates them otherwise.
  - Existing customers keep their current status and history and get a NULL next review date. NULL shows as "due" until Finance sets dates in Settings or the import.
- **Fresh install**
  - `install/sql/tables/*.sql` and the `debtorsmaster.sql` columns.
  - `install/sql/data` edits: config, systypes, securitytokens, securitygroups (tokens 21 to Accountant and Sysadmin, 22 to Sysadmin), scripts, and menuitems for roles 1–9.
  - New data files `holdreasons.sql` and `dunningstages.sql`. Fresh non-demo installs previously had no hold reasons at all.
- **`install/sql/demo.sql`**: the Demo=Yes install skips `install/sql/data`, so the same rows are appended there. Statements are kept one per line and contain no semicolons, for `PopulateSQLDataBySQLFile`.
- **Not changed**
  - The legacy `sql/mysql/upgrade*.sql` chain, which is only for old versions.
  - The stale, unread `sql/demo.sql`.
  - No GL triggers are needed.

## Decisions on the open questions and other choices

1. **Interest**: a simple annual rate charged monthly (rate ÷ 12) on the overdue balance net of unallocated cash. It is the same in every currency. A statutory rate can be entered as the rate.
2. **Late fee**: one flat fee per customer per month, set in home currency and converted at the current rate into the customer's currency.
3. **No interest on interest or fees** (types 13/14 are excluded from the basis). Disputed items are excluded from interest and from reminders (BR-18). Charges are posted at the month-end date. No tax is applied to interest or fees.
4. **Final notice**: the customer is not put on stop automatically. The credit control report flags "final notice sent – decide whether to stop".
5. **Over-limit orders** from every route are accepted but held. "Over limit" is based on the balance plus open orders, the same basis as `GetCreditAvailable`. Holding is controlled by `CreditHoldOverLimit` and is independent of the existing `CheckCreditLimits` warn/prohibit setting. A released order that is later increased is held again.
6. **Write-offs**: one approver, the token-22 holder. The requester cannot approve their own write-off. The limit defaults to 1,000 in home currency; Finance sets the real figure. The Financial Accountant does not also need to sign off. The write-off is posted at today's rate and allocated to the invoices, and the currency difference is realised through `salesexchangediffact`, as `CustomerAllocations.php` does. The debtors control account therefore clears exactly.
7. **Written-off debt later paid**: credit control records a "recovery" (type 47, crediting the bad debt account) and the receipt is allocated against it.
8. **Reps see the reason** for a stop. User story 4 asks to know why.
9. **Letters are English only** (one set of wording); translations are a later change.
10. **Watch is not shown** in the portal; customers only see "on hold" or "open".
11. **Cover when both controllers are away**: the administrator grants token 21 temporarily. Everything is logged per user.
12. **Credit limit is per customer** (`debtorsmaster`), shared by all branches, as webERP already does. There is no head-office grouping.
13. **Reminders**
    - One stage at a time.
    - The stage is based on the items still unpaid from the last letter; new overdue items start again at stage 1.
    - The minimum gap between letters is set in Settings (default 7 days).
    - Customers who have paid but whose cash is unallocated are not chased.
    - The recipients are the contacts flagged for statements (the accounts contact).
14. **Defaults are safe** (BR-41): interest 0, fee 0 and empty GL accounts. Nothing is charged, and no write-off is posted, until Finance sets them up. Invoices, statements and postings are unchanged for customers who are not overdue.

## Known limits and things not changed

- `EDIProcessOrders.php` has an existing `if ($CreateOrder = true)` assignment bug. I left it as it is; the stop check is a separate condition.
- `CounterSales.php` (cash sales against a location's cash customer) and `api_debtortransactions` `InsertSalesInvoice` (bookkeeping only) are not credit-checked.
- `Z_ImportDebtors.php` updates of existing customers can still overwrite the limit and status. It needs token 15, whose holders get token 21 anyway.
- The job that sets next review dates in bulk does not write a history row per customer.
- Nothing has been run. There was no environment to test against, so the PHP and SQL above are untested.

# Credit control – implementation notes

This is the credit control capability from `task/brd.md`. It covers credit reviews, stop and watch, credit holds on orders from every route, reminder letters, month-end interest and fees, bad-debt write-offs with approval, reporting, the customer portal, month-end reconciliation, install/upgrade, and the staff guide.

## How it fits webERP

webERP already had a credit status. Each customer has a hold reason (`debtorsmaster.holdreason` → `holdreasons`). The hold reason's `dissallowinvoices` flag means **1 = on stop** and **2 = watch**. Anything else (0, or the table default −1) means normal.

Order entry, `CustomerAccount`, `AgedDebtors` ("held only") and the API already read this flag. I kept it as the one source of truth rather than adding a parallel status. Credit control moves customers between hold reasons, and every move goes through one function that records who, when and why.

All the shared logic is in `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php`. Every route and page calls it, so the rules are applied the same way everywhere.

## What was built

### New tables

Each table is in `install/sql/tables/` and also in `sql/updates/44.php`:

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `custcreditreviews` | Credit reviews (immutable). |
| `custcreditevents` | Per-customer credit control history / audit trail (BR-32). |
| `creditorderholds` | One row per order that is held (over limit / stop), released, or noted (watch). |
| `dunningstages` | Reminder stages. |
| `dunningletters` | Letters sent. |
| `dunninglettertrans` | The items each letter covered. |
| `debtortransdisputes` | Disputed invoices. |
| `creditcharges` | Month-end charges. A unique key on (customer, period, type) stops a month being charged twice. |
| `creditwriteoffs`, `creditwriteoffitems` | Write-off requests, approvals and postings. |

New columns on `debtorsmaster`: `nextreviewdate`, `interestexempt`, `feeexempt`.

### New transaction types (`systypes`)

| Type | Name |
|---|---|
| 13 | Interest Charge |
| 14 | Late Payment Fee |
| 45 | Credit Control Charge Waiver |
| 46 | Bad Debt Write Off |
| 47 | Bad Debt Recovered |

They are separate types so that charges appear on accounts and statements as clearly described items (BR-21). It also stops them being mistaken for invoices: `PrintCustTrans` and `Z_SalesIntegrityCheck` assume a type 10 has a sales order.

### New security tokens

- **21 Credit control** – the credit controller and deputy.
- **22 Credit control approvals** – the Finance Director.

### New pages

All pages are on the AR menu and registered in `scripts`.

| Page | Token | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `CreditControl.php` | 2 | Customer credit hub. Shows position and history. Credit control can record reviews, change status, set exemptions, mark disputes and add notes. Reps see their own customers only, read-only. |
| `CreditOrderHolds.php` | 21 | Held orders, orders of stopped customers, and watch orders. Credit control releases orders here. |
| `DunningStages.php` | 21 | Stages, days overdue and wording. |
| `DunningRun.php` | 21 | Preview, exclude, send by email; customers without email are listed to post. |
| `DunningLetter.php` | 1 | View or print a letter. A customer login sees only its own. |
| `CreditCharges.php` | 21 | Preview and post month-end interest and fees; waive a charge. |
| `CreditWriteOff.php` | 21 | Write-off request or post, put on stop, record a recovery. |
| `CreditWriteOffApprove.php` | 22 | Approve or reject write-offs over the limit. |
| `CreditWriteOffReport.php` | 21 | BR-29. |
| `CreditControlReport.php` | 2 | BR-30. |
| `CreditControlSettings.php` | 10 | Finance's parameters, plus bulk next-review dates for go-live. |
| `CreditStatusImport.php` | 21 | Loads the spreadsheet stop list, limits and review dates (BR-40). |
| `DebtorsControlReconciliation.php` | 8 | BR-37/38. |

### Staff guide

- New `doc/Manual/ManualCreditControl.html` covers every 4.1 item and includes a "For sales staff" section (BR-43).
- Added to `ManualOutline.php`.
- `ManualCreditStatus.html` is updated.

## Existing code changed, and why

### Order routes (BR-06/08/10/11)

- **`DeliveryDetails.php`** is the single commit point for sales-office and web-shop orders.
  - It refuses orders for customers on stop. Quotations are still allowed.
  - After insert or update it calls `EvaluateOrderCredit()`, which holds an order that takes the customer over the limit and notes an order for a watch customer.
  - Customer logins get "awaiting approval" or "account on hold" messages.
- **`SelectOrderItems.php`**
  - Shows the status banner, including when modifying an order.
  - Web-shop customers on stop are told and stopped.
  - Watch is no longer shown to customers.
  - The customer-login path tested `dissallowinvoices == 0`. That treated the default −1 as "on hold", so I changed it to `!= 1`.
- **`ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`**, **`GeneratePickingList.php`**, **`PDFPickingList.php`**
  - These refuse or skip orders that are held, or whose customer is on stop, unless credit control has released the order.
  - `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` checks again at posting time.
- **`RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php`**
  - Skips templates of stopped customers without advancing `lastrecurrence`, so the order is raised on the first run after the stop is lifted.
  - Evaluates new orders, and does not auto-invoice a held order.
- **`EDIProcessOrders.php`**
  - Does not create orders for stopped customers, says why in the advice email, and logs it.
  - Evaluates created orders.
- **API**
  - `api_php.php` includes the library.
  - New error codes 1174–1176.
  - `InsertSalesOrderHeader` refuses stopped customers.
  - `InsertSalesOrderLine` and `ModifySalesOrderLine` evaluate the order and return `OrderHeldForCreditApproval` in `$Errors[1]` when it is held.
  - `InvoiceSalesOrder` refuses held or stopped orders.
  - `InsertCustomer` sets the next review date.
  - `ModifyCustomer` only lets token-21 users change `creditlimit` or `holdreason`, and records the change.

### Who may change limits and status (BR-07/34)

- **`Customers.php`**
  - Limit and credit status are read-only without token 21. Changes made by credit control go through the logging functions.
  - New customers get a next review date (BR-02) and an "opened" history entry.
  - A customer with credit history cannot be deleted.
- **`CreditStatus.php`**
  - Moved to token 21. The codes decide who is stopped.
  - A Normal/Watch/Stop select replaces the checkbox. The checkbox could only store 0/1, so saving a watch code silently reset it to normal.

### Visibility (BR-09/31/33/35/36)

- **`SelectCustomer.php`**: status banner and a link to Credit Control.
- **`CustomerInquiry.php`** and **`CustomerAccount.php`**
  - Status banner. "ACCOUNT ON HOLD" now shows only for status 1; it showed for watch and −1 too.
  - A customer login is forced to its own `www_users.customerid`. Before this, a customer could pass any `?CustomerID=` (BR-36).
  - Customers do not see watch or the reasons.
- **`CustomerAccount.php`** (also the portal "Account Status" page)
  - It only rendered types 10/11/12, so it now lists other types too (charges, waivers, write-offs).
  - New sections for reminder letters sent and charges (BR-35).
- **`AgedDebtors.php`**: credit status, credit limit and last reminder columns.

### Ledger agreement (BR-37/38)

`Z_CheckDebtorsControl.php` only counted types 10/11/12, so the new types would have shown as differences. It now has an "Other" column. The new reconciliation page is the main tool.

### Other existing files

- **`Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php`**: copies the new `debtorsmaster` columns and renames the new tables.
- **`Z_ImportDebtors.php`**: imported customers get a next review date.

## Install and upgrade (BR-39/40)

Following the map's hazard that schema lives in several places, each change is in all of them:

- **`sql/updates/44.php`**: tables, columns, systypes, tokens, scripts, config, menu items and reminder stages. It is guarded by `Errors == 0`.
  - Tokens 21/22 go to every role that already holds token 15 (administrators). The administrator then assigns them to the credit controllers' and Finance Director's roles.
  - It reuses existing watch, stop and normal hold reasons if the company has them, and creates them otherwise.
  - Existing customers keep their current status and history and get a NULL next review date. NULL shows as "due" until Finance sets dates in Settings or the import.
- **Fresh install**
  - `install/sql/tables/*.sql` and the `debtorsmaster.sql` columns.
  - `install/sql/data` edits: config, systypes, securitytokens, securitygroups (tokens 21 to Accountant and Sysadmin, 22 to Sysadmin), scripts, and menuitems for roles 1–9.
  - New data files `holdreasons.sql` and `dunningstages.sql`. Fresh non-demo installs previously had no hold reasons at all.
- **`install/sql/demo.sql`**: the Demo=Yes install skips `install/sql/data`, so the same rows are appended there. Statements are kept one per line and contain no semicolons, for `PopulateSQLDataBySQLFile`.
- **Not changed**
  - The legacy `sql/mysql/upgrade*.sql` chain, which is only for old versions.
  - The stale, unread `sql/demo.sql`.
  - No GL triggers are needed.

## Decisions on the open questions and other choices

1. **Interest**: a simple annual rate charged monthly (rate ÷ 12) on the overdue balance net of unallocated cash. It is the same in every currency. A statutory rate can be entered as the rate.
2. **Late fee**: one flat fee per customer per month, set in home currency and converted at the current rate into the customer's currency.
3. **No interest on interest or fees** (types 13/14 are excluded from the basis). Disputed items are excluded from interest and from reminders (BR-18). Charges are posted at the month-end date. No tax is applied to interest or fees.
4. **Final notice**: the customer is not put on stop automatically. The credit control report flags "final notice sent – decide whether to stop".
5. **Over-limit orders** from every route are accepted but held. "Over limit" is based on the balance plus open orders, the same basis as `GetCreditAvailable`. Holding is controlled by `CreditHoldOverLimit` and is independent of the existing `CheckCreditLimits` warn/prohibit setting. A released order that is later increased is held again.
6. **Write-offs**: one approver, the token-22 holder. The requester cannot approve their own write-off. The limit defaults to 1,000 in home currency; Finance sets the real figure. The Financial Accountant does not also need to sign off. The write-off is posted at today's rate and allocated to the invoices, and the currency difference is realised through `salesexchangediffact`, as `CustomerAllocations.php` does. The debtors control account therefore clears exactly.
7. **Written-off debt later paid**: credit control records a "recovery" (type 47, crediting the bad debt account) and the receipt is allocated against it.
8. **Reps see the reason** for a stop. User story 4 asks to know why.
9. **Letters are English only** (one set of wording); translations are a later change.
10. **Watch is not shown** in the portal; customers only see "on hold" or "open".
11. **Cover when both controllers are away**: the administrator grants token 21 temporarily. Everything is logged per user.
12. **Credit limit is per customer** (`debtorsmaster`), shared by all branches, as webERP already does. There is no head-office grouping.
13. **Reminders**
    - One stage at a time.
    - The stage is based on the items still unpaid from the last letter; new overdue items start again at stage 1.
    - The minimum gap between letters is set in Settings (default 7 days).
    - Customers who have paid but whose cash is unallocated are not chased.
    - The recipients are the contacts flagged for statements (the accounts contact).
14. **Defaults are safe** (BR-41): interest 0, fee 0 and empty GL accounts. Nothing is charged, and no write-off is posted, until Finance sets them up. Invoices, statements and postings are unchanged for customers who are not overdue.

## Known limits and things not changed

- `EDIProcessOrders.php` has an existing `if ($CreateOrder = true)` assignment bug. I left it as it is; the stop check is a separate condition.
- `CounterSales.php` (cash sales against a location's cash customer) and `api_debtortransactions` `InsertSalesInvoice` (bookkeeping only) are not credit-checked.
- `Z_ImportDebtors.php` updates of existing customers can still overwrite the limit and status. It needs token 15, whose holders get token 21 anyway.
- The job that sets next review dates in bulk does not write a history row per customer.

content.text:
I've built the whole credit control feature as files, but none of it has been run or tested, since there was nothing to run against. `NOTES.md` at the repository root records what was built and where, every existing file changed and why, and how each open question in the BRD was decided.

**The approach.** webERP already had a credit status: each customer's hold reason carries a flag (1 = on stop, 2 = watch). I kept that as the single source of truth rather than adding a second status. All the rules live in one new shared file, `includes/CreditControlFunctions.php`, which every order route and page calls. Every credit decision goes through it and is written to a per-customer history table that cannot be edited (BR-32).

**What it covers:**
- **Stop, watch and over-limit holds on every order route:**
  - sales office entry, the web shop customer login and the API: stopped customers are refused; over-limit orders are accepted but held; watch orders are flagged
  - EDI orders: refused for stopped customers, with the reason in the advice email
  - standing orders: skipped while a customer is on stop
  - dispatch, invoicing and picking lists: refuse held orders, and orders of stopped customers, until credit control releases them
- **Who can change things:** a new "Credit control" token is required to change limits or status, and a separate "approvals" token for write-offs over the limit. The customer maintenance screen, the credit status codes page and the API all enforce this. Sales reps only see their own customers, read-only.
- **New pages:**
  - the customer credit control page: reviews, status changes, disputes, exemptions, history
  - held orders, with release
  - reminder stages and the weekly reminder run (preview, leave customers out, email or list for posting)
  - month-end interest and fees, with preview, a "never charge the same month twice" rule, and waivers
  - bad-debt write-off, approval and report
  - the credit control report, Finance's settings page, a CSV import for the go-live stop list, and a debtors control reconciliation
- **Ledger:** interest, fees, waivers, write-offs and recoveries are new transaction types (13, 14, 45, 46, 47), posted to both the customer account and the general ledger. Each posting is checked to balance before it is committed.
- **Live system and new installs:** the upgrade is `sql/updates/44.php`. The same tables, settings, tokens, menu entries and transaction types are also in the fresh-install files and in `install/sql/demo.sql`, because the demo install skips the normal seed files.
- **Staff guide:** a new manual page, `doc/Manual/ManualCreditControl.html`, including a short section for sales staff (BR-43).

**Existing bugs I fixed because the feature depends on them:**
- A customer logged into the portal could see another customer's account by changing `CustomerID` in the URL (BR-36).
- The portal account page never listed anything other than invoices, credit notes and receipts, so charges would not have appeared.
- Saving a "watch" credit status code reset it to normal, because the form only had an on/off checkbox.
- Watch customers saw "ACCOUNT ON HOLD".
- `Z_CheckDebtorsControl.php` ignored all transaction types except 10, 11 and 12.

**Decisions you may want to revisit:**
- After the final notice, customers are only flagged on the credit control report, not stopped automatically.
- Interest is a simple annual rate charged monthly. The late fee is one flat fee per customer per month, set in home currency.
- There is one approver for large write-offs, and they cannot approve their own request.
- Interest rate, late fee and the GL accounts start at zero or blank. Nothing is charged or written off until Finance sets them up.
- Existing customers start without a next review date. They show as "due" until Finance sets the dates from the settings page or the import.
- On an upgraded system the new tokens go only to administrator roles. The administrator then has to give them to the credit controllers' and Finance Director's roles.

**Not covered:** counter sales and the API's bookkeeping-only invoice call are not credit-checked. The existing customer CSV import can still overwrite limits for its administrator users. I left an existing assignment bug in the EDI order intake (`if ($CreateOrder = true)`) untouched; the stop check is a separate condition next to it.
